data.review_body:
WORST refund process.  I bought 2 identical pairs of shoes, just in different sizes.  Neither fit and had to be returned.  Even though both pairs arrived to me TOGETHER, AliExpress made me return them separately (even though I began the return process at the same time).  I chatted with AA to express my concerns that separating the two pairs of shoes might cause return delivery issues, especially since AA had me return one pair via Fed Ex and the other pair via USPS.  My concerns turned out to be valid.  One return pair of shoes was received by AA and they refunded me.  However, AA claimed they did not receive the other pair.  Like I said, they should not have been returned separately since I received them together originally.  I had ample documentation from USPS stating that the items was delivered to the Linwood, NJ post office AND that the item was actually picked up by an individual.  As directed by AA, I even had my USPS receipt stamped with the USPS official seal and signed by USPS staff.  I had at least 3 disputes over this and at least 3 trips to USPS.  I sent AA reasonable proof that the item was in fact returned to the post office AND picked up by an individual.  It was not good enough for AA to refund me a crummy $11.82!  The would NOT have happened if AA permitted me to return both pairs together, just like they were delivered to me originally.  I have had to return many things over the years to Temu, Shein, Walmart, Amazon, Etsy, and Ebay and I have never dealt with such impossible requests.  Although the AliExpress chat teams have been professional and empathetic, I felt like they "yessssed" me to death, but did nothing.  I deactivated my AliExpress account and will NEVER do business with AA again.
Reply from AliExpress was for me to send them a packing video.  UNBELIEVABLE!

data.review_body:
I’ve been going in circles with AliExpress support for over a month now, and I’m writing this because at this point nothing else has worked.

The short version: I returned an item and paid for the return shipping myself, on the express understanding that it would be refunded. That wasn’t me assuming anything. Before the package even reached the seller, support told me in chat to keep the proof of payment because the shipping would be refunded once the return was complete. The return form in the app said the same. And the shipping cost was almost as much as the item itself, so if anyone had told me it was on me, I’d never have sent it back. It wouldn’t have been worth it.

Then it just became a wall.

July 7, they confirmed in writing: the shipping fee would be refunded based on the receipt. July 8, I sent the receipt, and there’s a logged reply on their side proving it. July 9, they closed the case saying they never got a valid response. That’s simply not true, and their own system shows it.

After that their escalation team offered a coupon as the refund format, and confirmed it twice, once on July 14. Issued within 1 to 5 business days if I replied within 24 hours. I replied on July 15, inside their own deadline. The coupon never showed up in my account. Not once. What I got instead was another email telling me no refund was possible at all.

So they promised, ignored my reply, closed the case for “silence,” then offered a coupon themselves, I accepted, and now it’s suddenly impossible. Every step of that is documented in their own emails.

What actually gets me isn’t even the money. It’s the lying. Different agents, same recycled lines, and a written promise from their own senior team that they’re now pretending never happened. A month of that.

If you’re reading this while deciding whether to buy from them: keep every screenshot, don’t trust a verbal or chat promise, and know that “we’ll refund it” can quietly turn into “policy says no” the moment the item’s back with the seller.

I still just want the coupon they already promised me in writing. That’s all.
data.review_headline: A month of broken promises over a return shipping refund

data.review_body:
This was a thoroughly unpleasant experience involving outright deception.
I bought a JBL speaker on AliExpress (order 3064127943454575) and received a crude counterfeit. The seller claimed it was the "Hong Kong version." I opened a dispute, and AliExpress ruled that I would get a refund upon returning the item. I shipped the item back at my own expense. Afterward, AliExpress changed its decision and demanded proof that the item was counterfeit—proof I no longer had, since I had already sent the speaker back. As a result, I was cheated out of both the cost of the speaker and the return shipping fees. To top it off, they completely removed the order and the associated correspondence from my purchase history.
data.review_headline: This was a thoroughly unpleasant experience involving outright deception
